text: Selecting one agent per job by weighted random selection appears efficient but is mathematically suboptimal for quality assurance, since expected quality equals only the reputation weighted average rather than the best available output.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6192998

isBasedOn.name: Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution

abstract: The Calcaterra-Kaal-Andrei framework selects a single agent per job through weighted random selection.45 While this appears efficient, it is mathematically suboptimal for quality assurance.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: reputation correlates with true quality only imperfectly
